previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, chronic lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis, obstructive sleep apnea, and prior DVT/PE on warfarin was admitted for worsening right leg swelling, pain, and shortness of breath. She had recently completed a course of clindamycin for cellulitis. Imaging ruled out DVT but confirmed severe lymphedema. She was treated with IV vancomycin for presumed recurrent cellulitis, diuresis with furosemide and home diuretics, and pain management. During admission, she developed oral and suspected esophageal candidiasis, requiring a 14-day course of fluconazole, which necessitated warfarin dose reduction and strict INR monitoring. Her PICC line was successfully exchanged due to malposition. By discharge, infection and swelling had improved, INR was therapeutic, and she was stable for discharge home with services and detailed follow-up instructions.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  BILAT LOWER EXT VEINS

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with lower extremity swelling// ?dvt

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed
on the bilateral lower extremity veins.

COMPARISON:  Lower extremity ultrasound ___..

FINDINGS: 

Limited evaluation due to body habitus.  There is normal compressibility,
flow, and augmentation of the bilateral common femoral, femoral, and popliteal
veins.  There is limited evaluation of bilateral tibial and peroneal veins. 
There is bilateral subcutaneous edema, primarily in the right calf, again
noted without definite organized fluid collection.

There is normal respiratory variation in the common femoral veins bilaterally.

IMPRESSION: 

Limited evaluation due to body habitus.  Limited evaluation of bilateral calf
veins.  Within this limitation, no evidence of deep venous thrombosis in the
right or left lower extremity veins.  Significant subcutaneous edema
predominantly in the right calf.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with poor access w/ multiple ___ PICCs
over the past ___ years.  Currently admitted with cellulitis requiring IV
vancomycin and limited peripheral IV access.  Spoke with ___ from ___
team recommending ___ placement as patient is known to ___// ___ placement

COMPARISON:  ___ line placement from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ resident and Dr. ___,
___ radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure and has
reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: 1% lidocaine was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues
overlying the access site.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  1 min, 5 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Single lumen PICC placement through the right brachial vein.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right
basilic vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set. Permanent ultrasound images were obtained before and after
intravenous access, which confirmed vein patency. A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire. The guidewire was then advanced into the superior
vena cava using fluoroscopic guidance. A single lumen PIC line measuring 48 cm
in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned
in the distal SVC under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was
confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest. The peel-away sheath and
guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured to the skin, flushed,
and a sterile dressing applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1.  The accessed vein was patent and compressible.
2.  Brachialvein approach single lumen right PICC with tip in the distal SVC.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a right 48 cm brachial approach single lumen PowerPICC
with tip in the distal SVC.  The line is ready to use.
